target.title: Back out WSL CA sync setup step
target.body:
## Summary

Backs out the Windows CA certificate sync setup step from PR #819. The feature was dead on arrival because it passed a multi-line bash script through the `wsl.exe ... bash -c` argv path while also relying on bash variables, so WSL expanded those variables before bash ran.

This removes:
- `SyncWindowsCaCertsStep` from the setup pipeline
- The CA sync implementation and helper record
- CA-sync-specific SetupEngine tests

## Validation

- `./build.ps1` — passed
- `dotnet test ./tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests.csproj --no-restore` — passed: 2697 passed / 31 skipped
- `dotnet test ./tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj --no-restore` — passed: 1579 passed
- `dotnet test ./tests/OpenClaw.SetupEngine.Tests/OpenClaw.SetupEngine.Tests.csproj --no-restore` — passed: 423 passed

## Real behavior proof

- `rg "SyncWindowsCaCerts|sync-ca-certs|WindowsCaCertificateExport|ExportWindowsTrustedRoots|update-ca-certificates|openclaw-windows.XXXXXX|windows-ca-certificates"` returned no remaining matches.
- `SetupStepFactory.BuildDefaultSteps()` now goes directly from `ValidateWslLockdownStep` to `InstallCliStep`; the broken CA sync step no longer runs during setup or uninstall.

## Not verified / blocked

- Local MXC E2E was attempted during the audit before this backout and failed on gateway startup with `EADDRINUSE` / systemd port conflict. This PR removes the CA sync path; gateway-mediated MXC proof should be rerun on a clean gateway port.
